key_insight: TriageRA-CCF uses source-only confidence, clinical coverage, and counterfactual signals to adaptively choose how much LoRA rank to activate per medical question.
clinical_relevance: This could help medical LLMs allocate more capacity to harder or less covered questions while keeping parameter-efficient fine-tuning lightweight.
method: Computes three supervision signals from source training data: base-model answer confidence, metadata-cell clinical coverage, and a close-miss counterfactual proxy.
Trains a straight-through budget router to select among active LoRA rank budgets {2,4,8}.
Adds budget-cost, entropy, and rank-balance regularization to stabilize routing.
evidence_signal: Across matched CMB-source training on Qwen3-8B and Llama3.1-8B, the method slightly outperformed LoRA, DoRA, and MoELoRA baselines, with modest average gains (+0.21 and +0.16 points vs the strongest external baseline).
watch_item: The improvements are small and not uniform across benchmarks or backbones, and adaptive routing may still be sensitive to stabilization and regularization choices.
paper_title: TriageRA-CCF: Source-Side Clinical Confidence and Coverage Signals for Adaptive Rank Budgeting in Medical LLMs
